clippings.speaker: Seth Rogen
clippings.quote: I mean, I couldn’t say enough great things about him. He’s the reason I’m not a homeless crackhead right now. Probably.
clippings.title: Interview with Seth Rogen
clippings.context: Responding to being told Apatow had raved about his writing, around the DVD release of Undeclared and The 40 Year Old Virgin.

clippings.speaker: Seth Rogen
clippings.quote: It was kind of the first legitimate thing a lot of us had really done, and the environment that Judd and Paul (Feig, the show’s co-creator) set was one of such camaraderie and working together and kind of communal attitude of making everything funnier… and it was a big influence on all of our lives.
clippings.title: Interview with Seth Rogen
clippings.context: On the bond among the Freaks and Geeks cast and crew.

clippings.speaker: Judd Apatow
clippings.quote: Seth Rogen, you know, we found him in Vancouver and he was just this odd, funny guy that, when we met him, was 16. … Then it turned out he was such a good writer that it was almost embarrassing, because his scripts were better than most everybody else’s scripts, and he was a kid, so we were all somewhat humiliated having him around.
clippings.title: Interview with Judd Apatow
clippings.context: Explaining how Rogen went from Freaks and Geeks actor to star and writer on Undeclared.

clippings.speaker: Judd Apatow
clippings.quote: Seth is one of the leads of the movie. And he kills so hard that I had to take some jokes out, because it was just weighing the movie in an odd way towards his character when it shouldn’t be that much about him. But people love Seth. I was very gratified, as a big Seth supporter, to see audiences really like him.
clippings.title: Interview with Judd Apatow
clippings.context: Just before The 40 Year Old Virgin opened.

clippings.speaker: Seth Rogen
clippings.quote: I didn’t know Judd when he was young so it’s kind of what I would imagine Judd would have been when he was young. Judd and I are very different — we don’t act anything alike. We are friends and we work together well but we are not very similar people.
clippings.title: Seth Rogen talks Funny People
clippings.context: Asked whether his Funny People character Ira was based on the young Apatow, for the film's DVD release.

clippings.speaker: Judd Apatow
clippings.quote: I saw The Studio and I was just blown away by what Seth and Evan had accomplished. … Like, wow, look how far they're taking it…. They're still getting better. It's incredible.
clippings.title: Judd Apatow chalks up his early career setbacks to being ‘cool enough to fail’
clippings.context: On Q with Tom Power, about the pride he feels as former protégés like Rogen and Evan Goldberg succeed on their own.

clippings.speaker: Seth Rogen
clippings.quote: At one time, when we were shooting ‘Knocked Up,’ we would improvise a lot, and we were improvising and Judd screamed from the other room, ‘Less semen, more emotion!’ … And honestly, as I’ve gone on to make films, it’s amazing how much I come back to ‘Less semen, more emotion.’
clippings.title: Seth Rogen Tells TIFF the Best Advice He’s Ever Received: ‘Less Semen, More Emotion!’
clippings.context: Onstage at TIFF before receiving the Norman Jewison Career Achievement Award, asked for the best advice from his mentor.

notes: NPR Fresh Air 2007 joint interview had no transcript on the pages checked. Rotten Tomatoes page date is its 2010-01-03 publish stamp (interview tied to the late-2009 Funny People DVD).
